questions.prompt: Beowulf ___ lift a heavy stone with one hand.
questions.explain: A modal is followed by the base verb: no -s and no 'to'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
choices: My friend cans run very fast.
My friend can runs very fast.
My friend can run very fast.
My friend can to run very fast.
questions.answer: My friend can run very fast.

questions.prompt: You ___ wear a helmet when you ride a bike.
questions.explain: 'Should' never takes -s and is followed by the base verb.

questions.prompt: Which question is correct?
choices: Can you help me with my homework?
Do you can help me with my homework?

Can you helping me with my homework?
questions.answer: Can you help me with my homework?

questions.prompt: We ___ play outside. It is raining too hard.
questions.explain: The negative of 'can' is can't or cannot.

questions.prompt: ___ open the window? It is hot in here.
questions.explain: Questions with 'should' use inversion: Should + subject + base verb.

questions.prompt: You ought ___ listen to your coach.
questions.explain: 'Ought' is followed by 'to' and the base verb.

questions.prompt: My brother ___ to get up at six every day. (has / have)
questions.explain: 'Have to' is not a modal: with he/she/it it becomes 'has to'.

questions.prompt: Which question is correct? (obligation)

Do we have to bring our own ball?
Do we must bring our own ball?
Do we have bring our own ball?
questions.answer: Do we have to bring our own ball?

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct? (future)

Will she able to come to the party?
Will she be able to come to the party?
Does she can come to the party?
questions.answer: Will she be able to come to the party?
questions.explain: 'Can' has no future form, so we use 'will be able to'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct? (wish)
choices: I would like to can swim like a fish.
I would like can swim like a fish.
I would like to able swim like a fish.
I would like to be able to swim like a fish.
questions.answer: I would like to be able to swim like a fish.
questions.explain: After 'to' we cannot use 'can': we use 'be able to'.

questions.prompt: Write the short form of 'cannot'.

Which sentence is correct? (past, no obligation)
choices: She didn't had to pay for the ticket.
She didn't must pay for the ticket.
She didn't have to pay for the ticket.
She doesn't had to pay for the ticket.
questions.answer: She didn't have to pay for the ticket.

questions.prompt: When the king was young, he ___ fight very well. (can / could)
Yesterday the thief locked the door, but the hero ___ open it and escape.
questions.explain: For one successful action in the past, we use 'was able to'.

questions.prompt: The hero fell into a deep hole, but he ___ climb out in the end.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is the most polite?

questions.prompt: Which is the most formal way to ask for permission?

May I ask a question, sir?

questions.answer: May I ask a question, sir?

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct for a polite request?

Do you could tell me the way to the station?
Could you tell me the way to the station?
Could you telling me the way to the station?

questions.prompt: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early.
